headlines.article_text: Walmart (WMT) Q3 2026 earnings Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points Walmart narrowly topped fiscal third-quarter earnings and revenue estimates. The retailer also raised its full-year sales and earnings outlook. The company highlighted e-commerce sales growth as it said it saw success with store-fulfilled pickup and delivery. In this article WMT Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT Shoppers enter a Walmart store in Charlotte, North Carolina, Aug. 30, 2026. Travis Dove | Bloomberg | Getty Images Walmart on Thursday reported earnings and revenue that narrowly topped estimates and raised its full-year outlook as it saw strong e-commerce growth ahead of the busy holiday season. "This was another really solid quarter for us, we feel good about it," CFO John David Rainey told CNBC. "We continue to gain share while continuing to improve the profitability of our digital businesses." Walmart said global e-commerce sales grew 17%, driven by store-fulfilled pickup and delivery, with Walmart U.S. up 23% and Sam's Club U.S. rising 30%. Its Walmart U.S. advertising business saw a 37% sales increase for the quarter. Rainey said that growth was driven by an emphasis on speed of delivery and lowered prices. He added that Walmart saw its largest share gains in the food category in three years during the third quarter. Walmart said it rolled back prices on nearly 8,000 products across its stores, a focus as U.S. consumers worry about the cost of living in the face of elevated food and gas prices. With the growth, Walmart also raised its full-year guidance, now expecting net sales to rise between 4.9% and 5.2%, compared to previous guidance of a 4% to 5% increase. Rainey said Walmart is maintaining "flexibility" in its guidance. Walmart anticipates adjusted earnings per share will come in between $2.84 and $2.89, compared with a prior range of $2.80 to $2.87. It's also now expecting adjusted operating income to increase between 8% and 8.6%, up from the previous outlook of between 7% and 8.5% growth. "We feel like, in the face of what has been kind of a volatile couple years between tariffs and high diesel prices, we've navigated this really well, which I think really underscores the durability of our earning streams," Rainey said. Here's how the company performed in its fiscal third quarter compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG: Earnings per share: 65 cents adjusted vs. 64 cents expected Revenue: $188.84 billion vs. $187.27 billion expected For the quarter ended Oct. 31, the company reported net income of $4.95 billion, or 62 cents per share, down from $6.14 billion, or 77 cents per share, the year prior. Revenue rose 5.2%. Walmart U.S. recorded net sales of $125 billion, up 3.6% from the year prior. Its comparable sales excluding fuel rose 2.9%, in line with Wall Street expectations, according to StreetAccount. Sam's Club reported net sales of $25.9 billion, marking a 10% increase from the year-ago period. It said its sales were driven by strength in the grocery category and general merchandise. The company is typically well-insulated from macroeconomic pressures because of its value reputation. Last quarter , the company said it was lowering prices of products across multiple categories, including beef. Rainey said on Thursday that he's "optimistic" about consumer spending heading into the holiday season and that the fourth quarter is already "off to a pretty good start." The big-box retailer has posted solid growth over the past few quarters as it sees customers gravitate to reduced prices, improvements in delivery and gains in its advertising business. It's also leaned into attracting higher-income consumers with its Walmart+ membership. In October, Walmart announced it was launching a joint membership option with Sam's Club as it leans further into convenience. Both stores will still offer standalone memberships, as well. Though the company reimbursed some members for the new membership rate, Rainey said it's already seeing positive returns on the joint model and that consumers are "spending appreciably more." The company on Thursday said its global membership fee revenue grew 17% in the third quarter. Shares of Walmart have fluctuated this year but are up roughly 13% year-to-date. "Our aim is to help humankind chart a safe course through this technological evolution, open new frontiers of discovery, and bring forth an age of miracles," Anthropic's co-founders wrote in the company's prospectus. "Everyone who owns our stock, whether an institution or an individual, becomes part of that effort." "The company uses safety branding to court investors, employees, and the public — even as it has quietly weakened its safety pledges and lobbied for self-serving regulation.
